pulls.title: Polishing -00
pulls.author: furry13
pulls.body:
1. Coping the Ack section from our doc and rephrasing it slightly.
2. Making per-body-aggregation explicit at the IANA level.
3. Rephrasing Security Section (I have some reservation re: RPKI in space so let's keep it out of scope)

comments.author: tony1athome
comments.body:
Hi Warren,

> -Additionally, addressing in space must be structured proactively to avoid the routing fragmentation that has historically plagued terrestrial networks. In the early days of IPv4 prior to the adoption of Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) {{RFC1518}}, address space was handed out in a disjointed manner, creating a sprawling, unaggregated global routing table colloquially referred to as "the swamp." If addresses for space missions continue to be assigned ad-hoc on a per-mission basis, the resulting patchwork will prevent route aggregation and impose severe routing table overhead on resource-constrained space hardware.
> +Addressing in space must be structured proactively to avoid the routing fragmentation that has historically plagued terrestrial networks. In the early days of IPv4 prior to the adoption of Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) {{RFC1518}}, address space was handed out in a disjointed manner, creating a sprawling, unaggregated global routing table colloquially referred to as "the swamp." If addresses for space missions are assigned ad-hoc on a per-mission basis, the resulting patchwork will prevent route aggregation and impose severe routing table overhead on resource-constrained space hardware.
> Interestingly enough, my main comment is around this first sentence -- "the routing fragmentation that has historically plagued terrestrial networks."
> 
> I don't really think that the current terrestrial network is "plagued" by routing fragmentation. Yes, I have a million or so routes in my FIB, but ¯_(ツ)_/¯.
> 
> I agree that there were serious concerns around RIB/FIB size and I've had to swap out hardware because I ran out of TCAM, RLDRAM or similar, but on the grand scheme of things this is quite far down on my list of sads...
> 
> If we changed "has" to "had", or simply dropped it altogether I'd be much happier
> 

Someone did a study and found that 1/3rd of the routes in the DFZ added no value (from their perspective).  They were simply more specifics that had the same next hop.  That’s 300,000 routes of garbage.

While I agree that there are bigger problems in the world, our job is to oversee this garden, and we’ve not been good stewards.

Tony

comments.author: wkumari
comments.body:
The vast majority of those are more specific hijack prevention routes.
It common to announce more specifics of a prefix, up to the commonly
accepted length (/24 in IPv4) to prevent someone else announcing it and
winning the longest-prefix-match. In theory, max-length in RPKI fixes this,
but partial deployment, etc.

As an example, I was on call during the Pakistan-YouTube outage. YT was
announcing a /22. Pakistan Telecom announced a /24 and so basically all
traffic followed their route - I quickly de-aggregated to /24s and the vast
majority of traffic came back (and also contacted PCCW and PT).

It's also really basically impossible to tell if a more specific is simply
a traffic-engineering route - I might be intentionally announcing a /20 to
AS65535 and a more specific /22 to AS65534 for TE purposes - from AS65530
there is no definitive way to know the more specific exists.

Anyway, yes, there certainly routes being announced that don't need to be,
but one can't really tell the purpose of the route without talking to the
operator (who quite possibly will just shrug and say "Dunno. Sue set that
up 12 years ago... and no-one wants to touch it because it's working just
fine...").

Interestingly enough, my main comment is around this first sentence -- "the routing fragmentation that has historically plagued terrestrial networks."

I don't really think that the current terrestrial network is "plagued" by routing fragmentation.  Yes, I have a million or so routes in my FIB, but ¯\_(ツ)_/¯.

I agree that there **were** serious concerns around RIB/FIB size and I've had to swap out hardware because I ran out of TCAM, RLDRAM or similar, but on the grand scheme of things this is quite far down on my list of sads...

If we changed "has" to "had", or simply dropped it altogether I'd be much happier.
